title: A Flock of Sheep Drinking at a Pool, with a Bullock and a Dog
recordTitle: A Flock of Sheep Drinking at a Pool, with a Bullock and a Dog
medium: Pen and black ink, gray wash

altText: A pen-and-wash drawing of a flock of sheep crowding at a pool to drink, with a bullock and a dog nearby.

source.verifiedBy: Met Collection API object record: title, artist, date, medium, public-domain flag, credit line, tags (Dogs, Sheep, Drinking), classification (Drawings) and image URLs read from the record

context: A drawing by the Venetian artist Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, dated by the museum to after 1763. He was the son and assistant of the painter Giambattista Tiepolo and made many lively drawings of everyday and pastoral subjects in pen and wash.

descriptions.k: A flock of sheep drinks at a pool. A bullock is there too. That is a young bull. A dog is nearby. They are drawn with black lines and gray paint. What sounds do they make?
descriptions.g12: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo drew these sheep long ago in Italy. They bend down to drink at a pool. A bullock and a dog are there too. He used black ink lines and gray wash, which is watery paint. Which animal do you look at first? Why?
descriptions.g35: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo came from a family of Venetian painters, and he also drew animals and country scenes. In this drawing, a flock of sheep drinks at a pool while a bullock and a dog stay close. He used pen and black ink for lines and gray wash for soft shadows. How does he show the sheep as a group and as individual animals?
descriptions.g68: This drawing from after 1763 shows sheep drinking at a pool, joined by a bullock and a dog. Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo uses quick pen lines for outlines and gray wash for shadow, which gives the animals weight with very few marks. Notice how the crowded flock forms one large shape and how the drawing hints at a calm country moment. What do you think he found interesting about everyday animals?
descriptions.g910: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo, trained in his father's busy Venetian workshop, made many drawings of animals and country life as independent works. Here pen lines and gray wash describe a flock gathered at a pool, accompanied by a bullock and a dog. The economy of means, with a few lines and washes giving volume and mood, is characteristic of his drawing. How does the grouped arrangement create unity while keeping each animal distinct?
descriptions.g1112: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo's pastoral drawings sit between the grand decorative tradition of his father's workshop and a more intimate, observational mode. In this pen-and-wash drawing of sheep, a bullock, and a dog at a pool, the economy of line and wash conveys mass, movement, and a mood of ease. Whether such drawings were made as studies, as finished works for collectors, or both is a question for scholars. The sheet invites reflection on how little is needed to evoke a living scene.

teacherNote.context: Giovanni Domenico Tiepolo was a Venetian artist from a family of painters who also made many independent drawings. This sheet of sheep, a bullock, and a dog uses pen and gray wash.
directions: Have students draw a group of classmates or animals using only a pen and a gray wash.
Ask students to circle where line ends and wash begins and explain what each does.
Discuss why artists draw animals and country life, using this sheet as evidence.
